clue.text: Driver taking a hairpin must go this mad

definitions.text: Driver taking a hairpin must go this
definitions.meaning: a motorist on a hairpin turn literally travels around the curve of the road
slang for crazy or out of one's mind

explanation.surface: A warning that negotiating a hairpin bend will drive a motorist crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The literal sense is travelling round a curve; the idiom means crazy, a British colloquialism for insanity.

clue.text: Arrives in posh car at Oxford?

parts.note: a Rolls (Royce) is the classic luxury car
students are said to be up at university, Oxford being the archetype

explanation.surface: Someone turns up at Oxford University in a luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge is British usage for being in residence at the university.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up somewhere is a colloquial way of saying one has come or appeared.

clue.text: Colour of earth in Northumberland

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the place name that follows

explanation.surface: A question about the shade of the soil in a northern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: This brown pigment is made from a natural clay, so it is literally a colour derived from soil.

clue.text: River animal died — one to get hit by arrows

definitions.text: one to get hit by arrows

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon
a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: A creature in a river is killed, struck by arrows.
explanation.walkthrough: In pub darts the missiles are often called arrows, which turns the hunting picture into a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Players throw darts, informally called arrows, at this circular target.

clue.text: African accommodation for the nobs?

parts.note: a hut is simple housing
U stands for upper-class usage, the toffs or nobs

explanation.surface: A question about where Africa's upper classes might lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobs' is British slang for the posh; U (upper class) comes from a famous 1950s essay on class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the main ethnic groups of Rwanda and Burundi, a people of Africa.

clue.text: Tapestry showing great mob on the move

indicators.note: letters in motion are being shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A woven wall hanging depicts a huge crowd marching.
explanation.walkthrough: Most solvers know the word as a citrus or herb; it is also a coarse tapestry fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the citrus and herb, the word names a coarse woven fabric used for hangings.

clue.text: In the darkness rider bumps off king

indicators.note: to bump off is to kill, so the letter for the monarch is removed from the horseman

parts.note: a knight is a mounted warrior
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Under cover of dark, a horseman murders the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours after sunset are the period of darkness.

clue.text: Understand Conservative's loyal

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, plus the S of the possessive
true means faithful

explanation.surface: A remark that one should grasp that a Tory is faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret a word or sentence is to grasp its meaning.

clue.text: One brings news: gangster has infiltrated crowd

indicators.note: infiltrating means slipping inside, so the mobster goes into the crowd word

parts.note: a herd is a mass of people
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A news report that a mobster has slipped into a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger announcing tidings; also a common newspaper title.

clue.text: Blair tore around as one on a mission of freedom

definitions.text: one on a mission of freedom

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are tossed about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tony Blair rushes about, presenting himself as a freer of peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was the UK prime minister who backed interventions abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who frees others from oppression.

clue.text: It's good to wander through wood

parts.note: to rove is to roam

explanation.surface: A pleasant invitation to stroll among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of trees, a copse.

clue.text: Dress seen on the street, something flashy

indicators.note: the gown sits on, here following, the road abbreviation

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a robe is a gown

explanation.surface: A garment worn in public, drawing attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A light that flashes rapidly, as in a disco.

clue.text: Sort of music enthusiast, I sat around at front of arena

parts.note: a fan is a devotee

indicators.note: turning around makes the two words read backwards
takes only the leading letter of the word arena

explanation.surface: A music lover sits about at the front of a concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-form composition in music, like an improvisation.

clue.text: The old man facing shock maybe on return as social outcast

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: on return means the head-covering word is read backwards

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it, so shock is an example

explanation.surface: Dad, after a nasty jolt, comes home as someone shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns HAIR into RIAH; 'shock' is not a jolt but a mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rejected by society, an untouchable.

clue.text: Bits of leaf concealed in water streams

indicators.note: in places the word for hidden inside the water channels

parts.note: races are swift channels of water, as in a mill race
hid means kept out of sight

explanation.surface: Leaf fragments lie hidden in flowing water.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of rachis, the central stalk or axis of a compound leaf.

clue.text: Bounded, given command to get into bed

indicators.note: getting into means being placed inside the word for the sleeping place

parts.note: taken as written
an order is an instruction

explanation.surface: Someone told to go to bed is fenced in.
explanation.definitionFit: Edged or limited, as a field marked off by a hedge.

clue.text: Like modern equipment favoured for making drug

parts.note: modern gadgets are digital rather than analogue
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Up-to-date technology is preferred in manufacturing a medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart medicine extracted from foxglove.

clue.text: A right fool interrupting the woman — one making unwelcome advances

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the pronoun

parts.note: her refers to a female
an ass is an idiot

explanation.surface: An idiot butts in on a woman, pestering her.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pesters or torments, especially sexually.

clue.text: A right bounder, man appearing to be rustic

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A scoundrel turns out to be a country bumpkin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' and 'cad' are old British words for a man who behaves badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Arcadia, idealised pastoral countryside.

clue.text: A cold church with saints in the entrance

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A chilly church has statues of saints in its doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A way in or approach to somewhere.

clue.text: Assented to a selfish craving

parts.note: greed is an excessive desire for more

explanation.surface: Someone gives in to an avaricious urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Consented or went along with something.

clue.text: Noise by female ending in eating area

parts.note: a din is a loud racket
-ette is a suffix marking the feminine, as in usherette

explanation.surface: A racket made by a woman finishing her meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room or alcove where meals are taken.

clue.text: Gossip is malicious woman with internal difficulty

indicators.note: the snag sits internally, inside the word for the spiteful woman

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful woman
a hitch is a snag

explanation.surface: Idle talk comes from a spiteful woman who has her own problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Light informal talk, small talk.

clue.text: Resin needs to be firm, mate

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Advice that a sticky substance requires a solid partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard tree resin used in varnishes.

clue.text: Wrongly taken garment has name on it

indicators.note: the letter is added on to the end of the shawl

parts.note: a stole is a shawl

explanation.surface: A pilfered wrap is marked with its owner's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is taking without right, so the item is pilfered.

clue.text: Caterpillar perhaps showing some cellular variation

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A caterpillar shows some variation in its cells.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is the immature form of a butterfly or moth, an example of this stage.

clue.text: A particular hairstyle for each maiden

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A hairdresser offers one style for every young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent wave, a curled hairstyle set chemically.

clue.text: Search succeeded — cry afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards places the tearful word after the abbreviation

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
to weep is to shed tears

explanation.surface: A hunt was successful, followed by tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough hunt, as in a police sweep of an area.

clue.text: Awfully smart woman brought in? Be suspicious

indicators.note: bringing in puts the woman inside the jumbled letters
awfully signals that the letters of smart are badly jumbled

parts.note: Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A terribly well-dressed woman shows up, raising eyebrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' reads as well dressed, but 'Awfully' makes it anagram fodder (SMRAT), and 'brought in' sets the woman's name inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to sense that something is wrong.

clue.text: Extreme believer is odd to natural men

indicators.note: odd signals the letters are rearranged strangely

explanation.surface: A zealot is out of step with ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic supporting papal authority beyond the Alps, so a hardline advocate.
